reviews.comment: I cannot stress how bad of a professor Lyuksyutov is. His lectures were always confusing and it seemed like he never came in with a plan on what he was going to teach us. On top of that, halfway through the semester he just quit showing up. Physics 207 is already a hard course, but he made it much harder to understand.
He's a good professor but physics is tough no matter what. Make sure you study the old exams and go to recitation. Going to SI sessions is super helpful, I got an A in the class because of them.

This was my original professor for PHYS 207 for the Fall 24 semester before he had to be replaced. His lectures were very unorganized and barely relevant to the material that we were supposed to be learning. He wanted us to discuss his own problems instead of teach and didn't know how to use any of the online resources he should've. Don't recommend
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Igor is totally unorganized and has no clue how to use technology at all (literally). You will not get anything from his lectures, so just learn the material using YouTube and the recitation material. Lastly, we didn't have canvas up and running until 4 weeks after we started the class. Igor is a nice man, but not at all suited to be a professor.

Mr. Lyuksyutov is the worst professor I have ever had. It took him four weeks to give us access to Canvas; his lectures are all over the place, and he doesn't have any actual notes that he bases his lectures on. He acknowledges his accent makes it harder to understand him, but this is the least of his problems. I could go on. Take Tatiana instead.

Man showed up to class with COVID19 while coughing on everything in sight. His lectures are mess of random information that is ultimately useless. I was in the class for two days a knew I was not going to pass with the way he was teaching the class. I genuinely don't know how this man has a job here.

too much to say: 
- 2 tests, and lab grades
- Igor does not teach students, he puts on harvard lecture videos
- no grades until the last day of semester
- falls alseep in class
- unreachable by email
- hard to understand, does not use mic
- attending class is pointless
- must teach yourself all concepts in class
overall ok class, ended with a 97.

Two tests and your six lab presentations r ur entire grade. At beginning of semester u have to form groups for lab; be wise who u choose bc ure stuck w them whole semester. The labs themselves r stupid easy, but at the end of the sem u have to turn in all six presentations so make sure they get done. Hes an angel, just pay attention in class.
Take him for summer physicss!!!!! Test were like pervious exams, lectures were not that hard to follow and labs were easier than 201. 10/10 would recommend.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does not teach. Only grades are exams. Don't try to ask him questions because he will not answer them, and all he does is play Harvard lecture videos. One time as student in class asked if he could work out the math problem to show us how to do it and he literally said he did not know how to.

Igor does not act like a professor. He will not answer questions and will not respond to any emails. He gives out no rubric for presentations and still tell us everything we do is wrong without any elaboration. For lectures, he struggles using the sound system and ends up playing a video he just skips thru. He heavily breathes into the mic :(.
He is an amazing man. If you hurt his feelings you are a mean person.

no homework or any assignments in the grade book besides two tests, the first midway test and the cumulative test, and lab presentations which are an auto 100 and so easy. the tests are beyond easy because he uses stuff from previous years that he gives you to study. its simple 8th grade calculations and igor is the nicest man ever. we cook in labs

If you aren't strong in math or science, RUN from this prof. Igor is a nice guy, but this class is the worst I've taken. I had to teach myself everything. I went to lectures but I couldn't understand his accent. He likes to talk without writing on the board, which can be confusing. All of his resources are spread out through multiple platforms.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Really rough Proff. Only goes through about 2 problems per class and it barely helps. Your mostly going to be teaching yourself all the content and there is tons of homework staggered in a way where you will have 15 assignments due on one day. Best advice is to get a tutor early and work hard in recitation so you can actually learn some stuff.

Igor is an awesome dude. He has a pretty thick accent but you can still understand him. This class is the easiest science class ever and is very simple (8th grade level easy). The labs are fun, you get to make things like jello and flan. 1 midterm and a cumulative final, very easy. Non-stem majors take this class for an easy A science credit.
Do NOT take Igor. You will teach yourself everything and rely on the review of other profs. Takes at least a week to grade a multiple choice test, and going to class is pointless.

His lectures consist of him putting a problem on the board and expecting you to already know how to get the answer. As someone who had absolutely no physics experience before taking this course, the lectures were a waste of time. I ended up reading the book and going through the practice exams to make a decent grade. He's a nice guy but a bad prof.

Consistently showed up to class late. Would do the problems on the board incorrectly, and when asked how to solve them would say, "I don't know." While he is a nice person, as a professor, he should not be allowed to teach this type of course. The few homework's he did assign was incredibly hard and his lectures are a waste of time. Avoid him.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Igor as a person is kind and respectful. However, as a professor, he is lazy and lacks any serious motivation to truly aid his student's learning. His lectures consisted of him rambling about unrelated topics. You are better off using the book and skipping lectures, but hey if you want to attend class just show up 10 min late like him.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He wasn't a good professor. Lecture consisted of "Oh if this was made this way, I would have been right" (he would get problems wrong on the board). I had to rely on the textbook alone the whole semester and even that wasn't enough (and I consider myself a pretty good learner). Get a good professor who will actually teach. Also, very unorganized.

Professor Igor is a lovely man, and clearly intended for the class to be an easy credit, but really grades you on three things: midterm test, final test, and labs. You'll never know what's going to be on tests because lectures are a waste of time. Passable if you really try, but not worth it. I'm usually a straight A student and I'm looking at a C.

Professor Igor does not teach, he puts on lecture videos from Harvard. It's pointless, I stopped going to class. The labs are mandatory, you do the lab, make a powerpoint, and then present it to the class. The exams are the same as his previous exams and he goes over those in class. Review those and you'll do fine on the exams (there's 2).

Prof. Lyuksyutov was confusing and unclear about due dates and instructions. He didn't seem to know much about what he taught, we spent over half of the class watching Harvard lectures off YouTube. Grades were heavily based off three exams with only ten questions each. Interrupted students asking questions in class and wouldn't respond to emails.

Igor is such a sweet prof. He has a very strong accent so sometimes it's a bit tough to understand but he tells you exactly what to do and if you listen to lectures you will get such an A. This class is as easy in person as online and doing the labs are so fun and easy (they're also optional and if you do them you get extra credit!!!) ily igor

Random attendance takes (not quite sure factor in on his mandatory attendance policy). Tests are easy if you go over his review problems, which he works through in class. Not necessarily disorganized but theres little structure in classwork. I never used the textbook but he provides a (free) link to it. For sure an easy A

He answers questions clearly, people just read too much into it because he tends to reword the question prior to him giving his answer. Accent Is thick but really not as big of a deal as people make it seem. Easy grader and states what material should be studied for exams. He works through each problem in class. Classwork is random other than this.
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Before registering for this class, I read on here that it was really easy and a good phys credit for non stem majors. I guess that may be true for the in person aspect for this class. With classes being online, he is very unorganized, everyone is always confused, is very unclear about things and then will give very short and confusing answersToQues
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Group projects

reviews.comment: - Class has no structure - No study material, no busy work - Strong accent - Little learning value (basic physics) - For tests, notes are useless (study old exams) - Grades (lab-completion, 2 tests) - If you want an easy A, but a risky A, this class may be for you. If you get anxiety from unorganized profs, it's a no. Note: COVID times
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I took this class over the summer online and it was horrible. You will have to teach yourself everything, he tests over concepts , but will never teach you them. Khan Academy is the only reason I did well. Class consisted of him working through 3 practice questions for an hour and a half. He may be different in person, but online was a nightmare.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He does an amazing job conveying a difficult topic to his students and wants them to succeed. I never trust rate my professor because many people who write reviews often are the ones who never applied themselves in the course and complain. if you do the provided practice problems and apply the concepts outside of class you'll get a good grade.

I have had bad profs, but he was literally the worst. He did not do anything to ever help his students, would email us at around 2 am and expected us to know everything before even taking the class. His lectures are him going over test material that was never on the test. Watched another profs lectures and Tutor John to get the grade

Igor started off being nice & helpful, but the class had no structure. Youll teach yourself everything on the tests, and he does NOT respond to emails often at all. Dont take if you want an easy A, its attainable but also caused much more stress than an entry level course shouldve. Attendance is a grade & communication is awful.

Professor Lyuksyutov is a very nice man! His class is really aimed at liberal arts students who want a very basic introduction to concepts in physics! The labs are the best part of the class, very interesting and fun! He will not let you fail this class, if you show up and try you will make at least a B but probably an A!! Also you get chocolate!!

Avoid at all costs. The class itself was not very difficult if you studied, but Igor's communication turned it into a study in frustration. 50/50 chance he'll respond to emails, was never in his office, didn't communicate with the TAs, was slow to correct grading errors (or do anything), and would introduce new material on the REVIEW days.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Hes a really nice guy, he can just be hard to understand sometimes since English isn't his first language. He does not try to make the class hard and writes very fair tests. If you can't understand his lectures, go to tutor John. He just goes over fords tests in class and then writes tests that are easier.

For physics 125 - soooo easy all you have to do is show up to class and labs for an easy A hell use clickers for attendance but hell ask us if something is too hard and if we say yes he wont put it on the exam and hes an adorable old man loved his class
The only grades are labs, a midterm, a final, and attendance through iClicker(but you only have to show up 75% of the time). The class is super easy AND you get to cook/eat for labs. 10/10 recommend

Alright so Igor is a super nice dude, but his teaching style did not work for me at all. I just went to A+ and learned there and squeezed by with a B. Igor did help as much as he could for people that were struggling to pass.

He started off helpful, especially during office hours, but towards the end, he was short tempered and rude. There's a lot of online homework, but the labs are really easy with no practical. In class, we go over practice tests, so the tests weren't too bad. As a person, he didn't motivate me and he was not understanding, always judged us
reviews.ratingTags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Igor is a great professor, he really cares about his students' success. Lecture is mandatory because you have clicker points that count toward a total attendance/participation grade. The homework is so much harder than the exams, but chegg is a great help. If you just take several of the previous common exams before the test, you will do well.

Igor spends lecture doing problems from Ford's old exams which are similar to our tests. If walking through examples isn't how you learn then this class isn't right for you.  Mastering physics hw answers are online. I had to go to SI sessions, Igor's review, and A+ tutoring to earn a B in this course. Physics is hard no matter who your prof is.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: It is very difficult to understand things without using all resources available to you. Sheer massive amounts of homework is very time consuming and, IMO, doesn't reflect exams. Igor was extremely helpful outside of class and cared about your success! Go to his help sessions and SI, and it shouldn't be too difficult.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The accent isn't that bad, but it's very difficult to grasp concepts without reading on your own. Homework is much harder than tests, and counts for very little.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Igor really doesn't get enough credit. We have common exams now, so he basically does practice problems for most of the class. That's good, since it helps you pass the exam, but if a concept is giving you trouble you'll either have to consult the book or go to one of his reviews (very helpful, btw). Also, he ALWAYS extends the homework deadline.
avoid if possible
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Poor Igor seems like a great guy; a Russian teddy bear. However, I did not learn a thing from him. His lectures are very disorganized. He never fully explains a concept before giving sample problems from another professors previous exams. He then fails to work through them completely. Be ready to read the chapters and pretty much teach yourself.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Igor is confusing and disorganized. Typically any explanation consists of writing something on the board and saying that it's very easy before moving on to something else's. Refuses to work a problem in its entirety on any occasion, even the first time is introduced. I attended Tatiana's class when I could  to learn the material.

Igor doesn't get as much credit as he deserves. He has a Russian accent and speaks in somewhat broken english, but it was not difficult for me to understand at all (seemed like everyone's biggest complaint). His lectures are VERY helpful, although miss 1 question on a test and your grade will drop substantially :-/ I loved him as a teacher though.
Fantastic teacher, though accent was interesting. Very thorough and I enjoyed his class. The procrastinators failed, but if you do your work you will be pleased. He know his subject very well.

Igor cannot express what he is trying to say in English. He fails to cover the overall concept of a lecture, much less mention out of all his lecture the important material, where "most" of the material is not important and mumble the most important concepts. You will not truly learn in his class. By guessing how to use equations, you can get a C.
Complete jerk. Argues with students and takes offense to even nice and innocent questions. Tests are extremley hard and Igor does not see it nessesary for a curve. DO NOT TAKE HIM.
